# ASN.1 DER differential tests

These tests compare our verified ASN.1 DER parser with three unverified
implementations:

* [asn1tools](https://github.com/eerimoq/asn1tools) (Python), with its `der` codec;
* [rasn](https://github.com/librasn/rasn) (Rust), with types generated by
  [rasn-compiler](https://github.com/librasn/compiler);
* [asn1-rs](https://github.com/rusticata/asn1-rs) (Rust), with types written by
  hand using its derive macros, since it has no ASN.1 compiler.

They run as part of `make -C src/ASN1 test`, and so as part of the toplevel
`make test`.

## Principles

* Each vector's expected verdict (`accept` or `reject`) comes from X.690 or
  X.680, and the vector cites the clause. It is never copied from our parser's
  output.
* A vector runs on an implementation only if every feature it is tagged with
  is `supported` or `partial` in that implementation's `capabilities/*.json`.
  DER strictness is not a capability: all three implementations claim to
  decode DER.
* Our parser must agree with every expected verdict. Any other disagreement
  is a *discrepancy*. Each discrepancy must be triaged (classified) in
  `triage/known.json`, so `make test` only fails on regressions.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `schemas/*.asn` | ASN.1 modules, the input for asn1tools and rasn-compiler |
| `../ASN1.DiffTest.*.fst` | F\* translations of the schemas |
| `../ASN1.DiffTest.fst` | name-based dispatch (`"Module.Type"`), extracted with the parser |
| `features.json` | the catalog of feature tags |
| `vectors/*.json` | hand-written test vectors: `id`, `type`, `hex`, `expect`, `clause`, `features`, optional `mutation`, `notes` |
| `gen/mutate.py` | derives `reject` vectors from the hand-written `accept` vectors, into `out/gen/` |
| `capabilities/<impl>.json` | per-implementation feature support, with the evidence for it |
| `triage/known.json` | triaged discrepancies: `impl`, `id`, `got`, `class`, `clause`, `rationale`, `upstream` |
| `harness/asn1tools/` | Python runner; `requirements.txt` pins the version |
| `harness/rust/` | Cargo workspace (`rasn-runner`, `asn1rs-runner`); `Cargo.lock` pins the versions |
| `report.py` | manifest assembly, report and gating |
| `out/` | generated: `gen/mutations.json`, `manifest.json`, `<impl>.jsonl` results, `report.md` |

Every runner shares one command line, `RUNNER MANIFEST RESULTS`. It writes one
JSON object per vector:

```json
{"id": ..., "impl": ..., "verdict": "accept|reject|unsupported|error", "consumed": ...}
```

The verdict is `accept` only if decoding succeeds *and* consumes the whole
input.

## Usage

```sh
make -C src/ASN1/difftest            # same as `check`
make -C src/ASN1/difftest check-all
make -C src/ASN1/difftest rebaseline
make -C src/ASN1/difftest clean
```

* `check` is the default, and is what `make test` runs. Our parser runs on
  every vector. Each other implementation runs only on the vectors that are
  not in `triage/known.json` for it. The filtered manifests and results go to
  `out/new/`. `check` fails if:
  1. our verdict differs from the expected verdict;
  2. a discrepancy is new;
  3. a baseline entry is still `untriaged`.

  Because the tool versions are pinned, the known results can only change
  when the harness changes. Skipping them can therefore leave a stale entry,
  but it cannot hide a bug in our parser.
* `check-all` runs every enabled implementation on every vector. In addition
  to the failures of `check`, it fails if a baseline entry no longer occurs
  (stale), or if its verdict changed. Run it by hand:
  * after bumping a pinned version (`requirements.txt`, `Cargo.lock`);
  * after editing a runner or a `capabilities/*.json`;
  * before `rebaseline`.

The full report is written to `out/report.md`. Its "skipped (known)" column
counts the known pairs that `check` did not run.
* `rebaseline` rewrites `triage/known.json` from the current results:
  * stale entries are dropped;
  * existing classifications are kept;
  * new discrepancies are added as `untriaged`. Classify them before
    committing.
* `clean` removes `out/`, `.venv/` and the Rust `target/`.

Toolchains:

* The `.venv` is created on first use, as in `share/everparse/tests/cbor`.
* The Rust runners use the ambient `cargo`, as in `src/cbor/tests_rust`.
* The first run needs network access to download from PyPI and crates.io.

Opt-outs:

* `ASN1_DIFFTEST_PY=0` skips asn1tools.
* `ASN1_DIFFTEST_RUST=0` skips rasn and asn1-rs.
* Without `cargo` on `PATH`, the Rust runners are skipped with a warning.

Implementations that were not run are not gated.

## Triage classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `harness` | runner or schema-translation bug (should be fixed, not recorded) |
| `manifest` | wrong expected verdict (should be fixed, not recorded) |
| `policy` | ours is deliberately stricter than X.690 |
| `ambiguity` | X.690 is unclear |
| `documented-leniency` | leniency documented by the implementation |
| `bug-asn1tools`, `bug-rasn`, `bug-asn1-rs` | implementation bug, with evidence in `rationale` |

A majority vote among the implementations is a hint, never a verdict.

## Coverage

Each type that some tool cannot handle sits alone in its own module, so the
other types still run.

| Schema | Types |
|---|---|
| `DiffSmoke` | the walking-skeleton SEQUENCE |
| `DiffPrim` | BOOLEAN, INTEGER, ENUMERATED, BIT STRING, OCTET STRING, NULL, OBJECT IDENTIFIER |
| `DiffRelOid`, `DiffIRI`, `DiffDesc` | RELATIVE-OID; OID-IRI and RELATIVE-OID-IRI; ObjectDescriptor |
| `DiffStrings`, `DiffStrings2`, `DiffVideotex` | the restricted character string types |
| `DiffTime`, `DiffTime2` | UTCTime, GeneralizedTime; DATE, TIME-OF-DAY, DATE-TIME |
| `DiffConstructed` | SEQUENCE with OPTIONAL/DEFAULT/IMPLICIT/EXPLICIT, SEQUENCE OF, SET OF, CHOICE, APPLICATION/PRIVATE and high tag numbers, nesting |
| `DiffSet` | SET (canonical order) |
| `DiffAny` | ANY, ANY DEFINED BY |
| `DiffExternal`, `DiffPdv`, `DiffCharStr` | EXTERNAL, EMBEDDED PDV, CHARACTER STRING |
| `DiffConstraints` | SIZE and value constraints |

Unsupported in each tool (see `capabilities/` for the evidence):

* asn1tools: RELATIVE-OID, the IRI types, VideotexString, EMBEDDED PDV,
  CHARACTER STRING. It runs with `check_constraints=True`.
* rasn: the IRI types, the DATE types, CHARACTER STRING, VideotexString,
  ObjectDescriptor. rasn-compiler maps EXTERNAL and EMBEDDED PDV to an
  untagged `Any`, so those are not run.
* asn1-rs: the IRI types, the DATE types, EXTERNAL, CHARACTER STRING, and
  constraints.

## Generated vectors

`gen/mutate.py` runs at manifest time. It derives `reject` vectors
(`mut/<mutation>/<base id>`) from every hand-written `accept` vector, using
mutations that break DER whatever the type:

* truncation;
* non-minimal lengths, outer and on the first component;
* a flipped primitive/constructed bit;
* a low tag number in the high-tag form;
* indefinite length;
* an extra `00 00` component;
* a last component that overruns its container.

Nested mutations skip opaque contents (ANY, EXTERNAL and the like). The
script docstring cites the X.690 clauses. There are currently 324
hand-written and 594 generated vectors.

## Findings

`triage/known.json` records each discrepancy with its evidence. The most
serious ones:

* asn1tools: an infinite loop with unbounded memory growth on a SEQUENCE OF
  element with the wrong tag (`intseq/reject/wrong-element`). The runner
  stops each decode after 2 seconds and reports `error`.
* asn1tools: the `der` codec reuses BER SEQUENCE/SET decoding. It accepts
  components in any order, ignores unknown and trailing components, and
  accepts indefinite lengths. Invalid strings and times escape as uncaught
  `UnicodeDecodeError`/`ValueError`.
* rasn: UniversalString contents are decoded as UTF-8. rasn-compiler
  generates RELATIVE-OID with the OBJECT IDENTIFIER tag.
* asn1-rs: a panic on an empty BOOLEAN (`bool/reject/empty`).
  `Oid::try_from` checks neither the tag nor the contents, so a NULL is
  accepted as an OBJECT IDENTIFIER. The SEQUENCE/SET derive ignores trailing
  components.
* rasn and asn1-rs ignore the primitive/constructed bit of most types, and
  accept low tag numbers in the high-tag form.
* All three: non-minimal lengths; unsorted SET OF; DEFAULT values encoded
  explicitly.

The `policy` entries are our 32-bit OID arcs.
The `ambiguity` entries are leap seconds, BMPString surrogates, and the
AlgId table constraint, which the plain `ANY DEFINED BY` schema cannot
express.

`triage/README.md` groups the discrepancies by root cause, with counts, and
drafts the upstream bug reports.

## Limitations

The tests compare verdicts only: a decode is `accept` only if it consumes
the whole input. They do not compare decoded values. Comparing values would need a common value
notation, such as JER (X.697), from every implementation. asn1tools and
rasn have JER codecs, but asn1-rs does not, and our extracted parser has no
value printer. So a decoder that accepts a valid encoding but returns the
wrong value goes unnoticed. rasn's UniversalString bug is caught only
because its UTF-8 decoding also rejects valid UCS-4 contents.

## Adding a test

1. Add or extend a module in `schemas/`.
2. Translate it to F\* in `../ASN1.DiffTest.<Module>.fst`, and add each type
   to the dispatch in `../ASN1.DiffTest.fst`.
3. Add each type to the dispatch in `harness/rust/rasn-runner/src/main.rs`,
   and translate it by hand in `harness/rust/asn1rs-runner/src/main.rs`.
4. Add vectors to `vectors/`, tagged with features from `features.json`.
   Each `accept` vector also yields generated mutations.
5. Run `make -C src/ASN1 test`, then triage any new discrepancies.
   Run `check-all` before `rebaseline`.
